name: Basic Electrical Engineering Lab
objectives: To introduce hands-on descriptions of various concepts of electrical systems and different laws and theorems, and to understand the mechanism of DC generator, DC shunt motor and three phase induction motor.
outcomes: Understand the characteristics of maximum power transfer and superposition theorems.
Analyze the efficiency of a single phase transformer by load test.
Analyze the load characteristics of a DC generator and the control of a DC shunt motor.
Understand KCL, KVL and Thevenin's and Norton's theorems.
Improve skills of team work, technical communication and report writing.
rule: A minimum of 08 experiments from the following
note:
Record format: aim, apparatus with ratings and range, circuit diagram drawn with a pencil and ruler, procedure, observation table, sample calculation, graph and result; note meter types (MC or MI) and least count.
Check the circuit with the teacher before switching on; keep rheostats at the safe position (maximum resistance in armature, minimum in the field of a shunt motor) at start.
In viva, be ready to say why a particular meter or connection is used, what the graph shape means, and the safety precaution for every machine.

exps.title: Verification of KCL and KVL
exps.aim: Verify that the algebraic sum of currents at a node is zero and of voltages around a loop is zero.
exps.apparatus: DC supply, resistors, ammeters, voltmeters, breadboard, connecting wires
exps.formula: KCL: ΣI = 0 at a node. KVL: ΣV = 0 around a closed loop.
viva: State KCL.
The algebraic sum of currents meeting at a node is zero; charge is conserved.
State KVL.
The algebraic sum of voltage drops and sources around any closed loop is zero.
Do these laws hold for AC?
Yes, when instantaneous values or phasors are used.

exps.title: Verification of Thevenin's and Norton's theorems
exps.aim: Replace a linear network with its Thevenin and Norton equivalents and verify the load current.
exps.apparatus: DC sources, resistors, ammeter, voltmeter, rheostat, breadboard
exps.formula: I_L = V_th/(R_th + R_L); I_N = V_th/R_th; R_th = R_N.
viva: How is R_th found?
Deactivate the independent sources (short voltage, open current) and find the resistance across the load terminals.
How are the Thevenin and Norton equivalents related?
V_th = I_N R_th, and both have the same equivalent resistance.
To what networks do they apply?
Linear, bilateral networks.

exps.title: Verification of maximum power transfer and superposition theorems
exps.aim: Show that maximum power passes to the load when R_L = R_th, and that responses from independent sources add up.
exps.apparatus: DC supply, rheostat or decade box, ammeter, voltmeter, resistors
exps.formula: P_max = V_th²/(4R_th) at R_L = R_th, efficiency 50 %. Superposition: I = I₁ + I₂ + ...
viva: State the maximum power transfer theorem.
A source delivers maximum power to a load when the load resistance equals the source's internal (Thevenin) resistance.
What is the efficiency at maximum power transfer?
Can superposition be applied to power?
No, because power depends on the square of current, which is nonlinear.

exps.title: Measurement of power in a three phase circuit by two wattmeter method
exps.aim: Measure the total power of a balanced three-phase load and find its power factor.
exps.apparatus: Three-phase supply, two wattmeters, three-phase load (lamp or inductive), voltmeter, ammeter
exps.formula: P = W₁ + W₂; tanφ = √3(W₁ − W₂)/(W₁ + W₂); power factor = cosφ.
viva: What happens to the readings at 0.5 power factor?
One wattmeter reads zero and the other reads the total power.
When does one wattmeter read negative?
When the power factor is below 0.5 lagging (or leading); its terminals must be reversed.
Does it work for unbalanced loads?
Yes, for a three-wire system with any load.

exps.title: Measurement of efficiency of a single phase transformer by load test
exps.aim: Load a transformer, measure input and output power at various loads and plot efficiency and regulation.
exps.apparatus: Single-phase transformer, autotransformer, wattmeters, ammeters, voltmeters, resistive load
exps.formula: η = (output power/input power) × 100 = V₂I₂cosφ/W₁ × 100; regulation = (V_NL − V_FL)/V_NL × 100.
viva: When is transformer efficiency maximum?
When the copper loss equals the iron loss.
Which losses exist in a transformer?
Iron loss (hysteresis and eddy current) and copper loss in the windings.
Why is efficiency high compared to rotating machines?
A transformer has no moving parts, so no mechanical losses.

exps.title: Determination of parameters and losses in a single phase transformer by OC and SC test
exps.aim: Find the equivalent circuit parameters, iron loss and full-load copper loss without loading the transformer.
exps.apparatus: Single-phase transformer, wattmeter, ammeter, voltmeter, variac
exps.formula: OC test: W₀ = V₁I₀cosφ₀, R₀ = V₁/(I₀cosφ₀), X₀ = V₁/(I₀sinφ₀). SC test: R₀₁ = W_sc/I_sc², Z₀₁ = V_sc/I_sc, X₀₁ = √(Z₀₁² − R₀₁²).
viva: What does the OC test give?
Core (iron) loss and the magnetising branch parameters.
Why is the OC test done on the LV side and the SC test on the HV side?
The LV side lets rated voltage be applied conveniently; the HV side has a smaller rated current, so lower-range meters can be used.
Why is SC wattmeter reading equal to copper loss?
The applied voltage is very small, so the flux and iron loss are negligible.

exps.title: Load characteristics of a DC generator
exps.aim: Plot the terminal voltage against load current for a DC generator.
exps.apparatus: DC generator coupled to a prime mover, field rheostat, ammeter, voltmeter, load bank, tachometer
viva: Why does the terminal voltage of a shunt generator fall with load?
Due to armature resistance drop, armature reaction, and reduced field current.
What is critical resistance?
The maximum field circuit resistance for which the shunt generator will still build up voltage.
What are the conditions for voltage build-up?
Residual magnetism, the field connections in the correct polarity and field resistance below the critical value.

exps.title: Speed control of DC shunt motor
exps.aim: Vary motor speed by field-flux and armature-voltage control and plot speed against field current or armature voltage.
exps.apparatus: DC shunt motor, field rheostat, armature rheostat, ammeter, voltmeter, tachometer, 3-point starter
exps.formula: N ∝ E_b/φ = (V − I_aR_a)/φ. Flux control gives speed above rated; armature control gives speed below rated.
viva: What happens to speed if field current is reduced?
Flux falls, so speed rises.
Why is a starter required?
At start E_b = 0, so the armature current would be very high without external resistance.
Why must the field circuit of a shunt motor never be opened?
Flux drops to residual value and the motor speed can rise dangerously.

exps.title: Study of running and reversing of a three phase induction motor
exps.aim: Start a three-phase induction motor, observe its running condition and reverse the direction of rotation.
exps.apparatus: Three-phase induction motor, DOL or star-delta starter, three-phase supply, tachometer, ammeter, voltmeter
exps.formula: N_s = 120f/P; slip s = (N_s − N)/N_s. Direction reverses on interchanging any two supply lines.
viva: How is the direction of rotation reversed?
Interchange any two of the three supply lines to reverse the phase sequence.
What is slip?
The relative speed between the rotating field and the rotor, as a fraction of synchronous speed.
Why is a starter used?
Starting current is 5 to 7 times full load, and the starter limits it.

exps.title: Calibration of a single phase energy meter
exps.aim: Compare the energy shown by a meter with the true energy and find its percentage error.
exps.apparatus: Single-phase energy meter, wattmeter, lamp load, stop-watch, voltmeter, ammeter
exps.formula: True energy = P × t; % error = (recorded − true)/true × 100. Meter constant = revolutions per kWh.
viva: Which principle does an induction-type energy meter use?
The induction principle; the eddy currents produced in the aluminium disc give a driving torque.
What is the meter constant?
Number of disc revolutions per kWh.
What retards the disc from speeding up indefinitely?
The braking magnet produces an eddy-current braking torque proportional to speed.
